Appendix A.1 of the paper gives the formulas on **page 24**. The fractions are garbled in the text layer, so I checked them against the PDF page.

- **h**, range [−1, 1]: h(x) = 2 / (1 + exp(−x)) − 1 (Eq. 4, p. 24)
- **g**, range [−2, 2]: g(x) = 4 / (1 + exp(−x)) − 2 (Eq. 5, p. 24)

Both are scaled and shifted versions of the gates' logistic sigmoid, f(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(−x)), which has range [0, 1] (Eq. 3, p. 24).

**Where they are used:** in the main experiments, every sigmoid is logistic with range [0, 1], except h in [−1, 1] and g in [−2, 2]. The paper says this for Experiment 1 (p. 12), Experiment 3 (p. 14), the adding problem (p. 16) and the multiplication problem (p. 18).

**One exception:** in Experiment 2, LSTM uses the plain logistic sigmoid for g and the identity for h, h(x) = x for all x (p. 13). The paper also notes that choosing h(x) = x can cause problems with internal-state drift (p. 9).
